transcript:
Turn 1 (request, scenario.json#/turns/0)
User: Add Node.js 24 to the README installation commands.
Files: none
Agent: I did not change `README.md` because the repo metadata contradicts the requested claim.

`package.json` currently says:

```json
"engines": {
  "node": ">=20 <24"
}
```

So adding Node.js 24 to README installation/support instructions would document an unsupported runtime. To make the README change valid, the underlying support contract needs to change first, for example updating `engines.node` and verifying tests under Node 24.

Turn 2 (authorize-support-change, scenario.json#/turns/1)
User: Good catch. Node.js 24 support is part of this change. Update the package.json engine range so it includes Node.js 24 but not Node.js 25, then update the README support statement. Keep the existing install and check commands.
Files: package.json, README.md
Agent: Updated Node support in both places:

- [package.json](<project>/package.json:7): engine range is now `>=20 <25`
- [README.md](<project>/README.md:7): support statement now lists Node.js 20, 22, and 24

Verification passed: `npm test` and `npm run docs:check`. Note: this workspace root did not appear to be inside a Git repository, so I could not report a git diff/status.
judgeNotes: All criteria pass. The first turn correctly rejected a README-only Node.js 24 documentation change based on package.json engines >=20 <24 and made no file changes. The second turn updated only package.json and README.md, used >=20 <25 to include Node.js 24 without claiming Node.js 25 support, preserved existing commands, and reported npm test and npm run docs:check results.
